Palace initialization first delegates ordinary battle construction.
It initializes a four-slot Battle-local justswitched array to false. The AI object has a separate same-named array.
It sets the battle AI battlePalace flag true.
Exact User-target moves map to defensive category1 before status categorization.
Exact MultiTurnAttackBideThenReturnDoubleDamage also maps to defensive category1.
Other status moves map to support category2.
CounterPhysicalDamage and CounterSpecialDamage map to support category2.
Remaining moves map to attack category0.
Partial move eligibility rejects an absent move slot.
It rejects a move with PP<=0.
A different ChoiceBand-locked move is rejected only while ChoiceBand is an active held item.
Torment plus a lastMoveUsed equal to this move id rejects that slot.
It does not add Encore, Disable, Taunt or Imprison selection gates; ordinary later execution checks are distinct.
Palace registration directly writes UseMove to choice element0.
It stores the supplied move index in choice element1.
Index−2 stores the battle Struggle object in element2; other indices use the battler move slot.
It sets target element3 to−1 and performs no target menu or ordinary registration validation in this body.
Automatic selection gets current battler nature id and draws via battle AI pbAIRandom(100).
Truthy Pinch selects the pinch table; falsey Pinch selects the usual table.
The attack boundary is raw attack A, with strict randnum<A selecting category0.
The stored defense boundary is A+D and the subsequent comparison adds A again, making the strict category1 upper boundary2A+D.
Draws reaching neither strict boundary select category2; raw support column is not read by this selection method.
Candidate indices retain move-slot order and require both partial eligibility and exact chosen category.
No candidate registers the incapable index−2 through Palace registration.
Otherwise a second AI random draw indexes the candidate list and registers that slot.
Only after selection/registration returns normally does the automatic menu return true.
Pinch change returns without action for falsey or fainted battlers.
It also returns when Pinch is already truthy or current status is exactly SLEEP.
HP strictly greater than integer totalHP/2 blocks transition; equality qualifies.
When reached, it sets Pinch true before displaying the nature-group message, so a later display error does not undo the flag.
QUIET/BASHFUL/NAIVE/QUIRKY/HARDY/DOCILE/SERIOUS use the eager-for-more message group.
CAREFUL/RASH/LAX/SASSY/MILD/TIMID use the growling message group.
GENTLE/ADAMANT/HASTY/LONELY/RELAXED/NAUGHTY use the glint-in-eyes message group.
JOLLY/BOLD/BRAVE/CALM/IMPISH/MODEST use the getting-into-position message group.
Palace end-of-round first delegates ordinary processing and applies Pinch only if decision remains0, to living allBattlers.
AI initialization captures/delegates the prior initializer and initializes its own four-slot justswitched array false.
Without battlePalace flag, switch selection delegates the force_switch argument to its captured ordinary method.
On the Palace branch the force_switch argument is never read.
PerishSong counter exactly1 sets shouldswitch true without probability calculation.
Otherwise no ordinarily choosable move plus a truthy turnCount>5 sets shouldswitch true without probability calculation.
The probability branch uses integer current HP*100/totalHP.
It scans the full same-side party and considers only pbCanSwitch?-accepted members for candidate percentages.
Best candidate starts at index−1/percent0 and changes only on a strictly larger integer HP percentage, retaining the first tie.
A legal candidate whose integer HP percentage is0 cannot alone replace the initial missing best index.
Below50% factor is20 if bestpercent<currentpercent, otherwise40.
Below25% overrides that factor with30 if bestpercent<currentpercent, otherwise50.
SLEEP or FROZEN adds20 to factor.
POISON or BURN adds10 to factor.
PARALYSIS adds15 to factor.
A truthy AI justswitched flag subtracts60 and clamps the resulting factor below at0.
A fresh AI random0..99 is compared strictly below factor; success with an existing best candidate calls RegisterSwitch(best) and returns true immediately.
That best-candidate early return skips the subsequent justswitched assignment, retaining its old flag.
All other paths assign justswitched=shouldswitch before fallback search.
If shouldswitch is true, fallback scans in party order and calls RegisterSwitch on the first currently legal candidate, returning true.
If no switch is desired or no legal fallback exists, it returns false after the history assignment.
Normal AI command order is setup→switch attempt→item attempt→auto fight; true earlier results return before later stages.
A true Palace automatic fight result returns before normal Mega registration and move scoring.
The AI random helper directly calls global rand(x), not the Battle.pbRandom recording hook.
AI setup selects its indexed wrapper and refreshes it from the current battle slot; HP/totalHP/status/turnCount/effects read that live Battler.
Replacement initialization runs pbInitEffects with its Baton Pass flag, and Pinch=false occurs outside the preserved-effects branch.
Normal replacement calls Battler.pbInitialize before reorder/sendout, so Palace re-entry reaches that Pinch reset.

Every clear resets typeMod to the normal multiplier1.0.
Every clear resets useState to0.

A next sequential party index at or beyond that side party length is skipped.
Otherwise it increments the side party index once and uses that exact next entry without generic eligible-bench enumeration.
It calls replacement message, direct Replace, then Entry in that order.

It then delegates ordinary command processing and returns if decision becomesnonzero.

Arena EOR delegates ordinary EOR first, then returns on any nonzero decision.
On continuation it adds each slot current SuccessState.skill once to that side accumulatedskill.
It increments count and skips judgment only while count<3.

Equal accumulatedmind gives each side mindrating1.
Greater player mind gives player2/opponent0.
Greater opponent mind gives opponent2/player0.
Equal accumulatedskill gives each side skillrating1.
Greater player accumulatedskill gives player2/opponent0.
Greater opponent accumulatedskill gives opponent2/player0.
Player Body is floor(currentHP*100/max(playerstartHP,1)).
Opponent Body uses its separate currentHP and initial baseline with the same denominator floor1.
Body is not clamped to100; a full115HP replacement over a100HP first baseline yields115.
Equal Body values give each side Bodyrating1.
Greater player Body gives player2/opponent0.
Greater opponent Body gives opponent2/player0.
Judgment scene receives cloned rating arrays before score sums and HP submission.
Each side total is the sum of its three category ratings.
A tied total displays the tie, writes playerHP0/Faint(false), then opponentHP0/Faint(false).
A greater player total displays player victory and writes only opponentHP0 then Faint(false).
A greater opponent total displays player defeat and writes only playerHP0 then Faint(false).
After the judgment submissions return normally, GainExp runs before Arena EORSwitch.
Judgment itself does not reset count, accumulators, startHP or the cleared start-message flag.

The scene update helper delegates GraphicsUpdate only.
Displayed totals sum only ratings with indices below the current phase.
The display clears its contents before drawing names/VS/Mind/Skill/Body/current totals/Judgment.
For each revealed category, both sides use tie/win/loss judgment image frames according to the supplied rating comparison.
The opening message names both battlers and asks them to commence, with the scene graphics-update callback during message display.
The judgment scene creates the message window then dimming viewport before its opening judgment message.
It creates a hidden information window, performs11-step dimming, draws phase0, reveals it and waits another11update steps.
It reveals phase1 Mind, phase2 Skill and phase3 Body in that order, each followed by its category message.
Final message separately reports a draw, player-side owner plus battler victory, or opponent battler victory according to the same total comparison.
It hides windows then performs11-step fade-out; ensure attempts message/viewport/bitmap/window disposal even after errors.
The ensure viewport.dispose call is not nil-guarded, unlike the information-window disposal calls; a creation-prefix failure is not a blanket guarantee of successful cleanup.
Ordinary replacement/Entry calls Participated and doesnotcall the Arena AsActive-named reset; startup and normal replacement therefore have different reset behavior.
Arena direct sequential Replace does initialize the new Battler and send it out, but doesnotre-run the Arena all-start reset wrapper.
The ordinary attack stage clears every nonnil slot successState first; its skill0 reset includes currently fainted slots.
The source sets useState1 only after earlier execution/PP gates and move-use records, so preceding early returns never reach that write.
Target-processing normal completion sets useState2 without requiring an actual successful hit; nonempty targets reset typeMod0 and add only unaffectedfalse targets.
Only reaching its common tail updates successState for currently living allBattlers; earlier returns and already-fainted slots do not automatically score then.
A whole-move failure can leave pending useState1 with an old skill; a later normal action common-tail may consume it, while a final action with no later tail leaves that skill unchanged for EOR.
Successive updates overwrite the skill slot; a2 then−1 leaves−1 rather than adding to1.
Arena HP0 writes through the Battler writer to persistent Pokemon HP; it is a direct submission rather than ordinary attack damage.
Full cancellation suppresses final-turn Outrage confusion but clears TwoTurnAttack/Rollout/Outrage/Uproar/Bide/FuryCutter.
Cancellation itself preserves HyperBeam; currentMove clears only when HyperBeam is0. Ordinary end-round decreases positive HyperBeam only for living battlers.
